hindi: झगड़े में पुरुष को मारने वाले के लिए वध विविध प्रकार का है।
english: For one who kills a man in a quarrel, the killing is varied.
notes: ghāta is rendered 'killing' (the act or the mode of putting to death) without deciding between the two; the following units give the grades. 'is' is a bare copula. ghnataḥ is the genitive of the present participle of √han.

words.gram: antar ind. + loc. sg. m. (loc. abs.)

hindi: सात रात्रि के भीतर मर जाने पर शुद्ध वध, पक्ष के भीतर सर्वोच्च, मास के भीतर पाँच सौ का और उठ खड़े होने का व्यय।
english: If [the victim] dies within seven nights, plain death-penalty (śuddha-vadha, literally 'pure killing'); within a fortnight, the highest; within a month, [one] of five hundred and the expense of [his] rising up.
notes: Elliptical: the nouns after 'highest' and 'five hundred' (daṇḍa/fine, and the unit of money) are not stated, so none is supplied in Hindi; English brackets only 'the victim' and 'his'. Whether 'highest' means the highest punishment/fine is not stated. śuddha-vadha is rendered literally 'pure killing' / plain death-penalty; the glossary has no entry, a reviewer should settle it for the chapter (also units 15, 26). samutthāna-vyaya: samutthāna is literally 'rising up'; the usual sense (cost of the victim's recovery or maintenance) is the alternative, not asserted. antar-mṛte is read as a locative absolute 'dead within (the period)'.

words.gram: pres. part. pra-√hṛ, m. gen. sg.

hindi: शस्त्र से प्रहार करने वाले के लिए सर्वोच्च दण्ड।
english: For one who strikes with a weapon, the highest punishment.
notes: src praharata = praharataḥ before uttamo (regular visarga sandhi).

hindi: मद के कारण हाथ का वध, मोह के कारण दो सौ का।
english: Through intoxication, vadha of the hand; through delusion, [one] of two hundred.
notes: hasta-vadha: vadha is 'killing, striking down, destruction'; the exact penalty (cutting off or destroying the hand) is not stated, so vadha is kept. 'Of two hundred': the noun and the unit of money are not stated. mada = intoxication (alternatives: pride, frenzy); moha = delusion (alternative: confusion).

hindi: वध के लिए वध।
english: For killing, killing.
notes: Literal. The first vadha is the offence, the second the penalty (death). Nothing is added to the Sanskrit.

words.gram: caus. pres. part. √pat, m. gen. sg.

hindi: प्रहार से गर्भ गिराने वाले के लिए सर्वोच्च दण्ड, औषधि से मध्यम, कष्ट देने से प्रथम साहस-दण्ड।
english: For one who causes a foetus to fall by a blow, the highest punishment; by medicine, the middle one; by torment, the first fine for rashness.
notes: Probably 'highest', 'middle' and 'first' are the three grades of the sāhasa-daṇḍa (the 'first' being the lowest), but the Sanskrit names the grade nouns only at the end; the translation keeps the literal order. garbha is masculine here. parikleśa = torment, harassing (the sense 'by distress/ill-treatment of the woman' is not asserted).

words.gloss: forcible killer of women and men
of the king's elephants, horses and chariots

hindi: बलपूर्वक स्त्रियों और पुरुषों के घातक, अभिसारक, निग्राहक, अवघोषक, अवस्कन्दक, उपवेधक, मार्ग और घर के प्रतिरोधक, राजा के हाथियों, घोड़ों और रथों को हानि पहुँचाने वाले, अथवा चोरों को शूलों पर चढ़ाएँ।
english: They should make mount stakes: those who forcibly kill women and men, abhisārakas, nigrāhakas, avaghoṣakas, assaulters, upavedhakas, robbers of road and house, injurers of the king's elephants, horses and chariots, or thieves.
notes: The e-text has a trailing '.-' at the end of token 1: the compound avaghoṣaka is followed by an unsandhied join to avaskandaka (the print has sandhi). The agent nouns abhisāraka, nigrāhaka, avaghoṣaka, upavedhaka are obscure; per the glossary approach they are kept untranslated, with only a literal gloss (abhi-√sṛ 'advance against'; ni-√grah 'seize'; ava-√ghuṣ 'proclaim'; upa-√vyadh 'pierce'), sense uncertain. avaskandaka from avaskanda 'assault' (glossary). pratirodhaka = robber (glossary 8.4); the literal sense is 'obstructor'. 'the king's' may govern all three of elephants, horses, chariots (taken so) or only elephants. stenān vā 'or thieves': it may instead qualify the whole list ('thieves, namely ...'); the literal word order is kept. The e-text 'hasty.aśva' shows hasti before a vowel (hasti-aśva).

hindi: और जो इन्हें जलाए या हटा ले, वह उसी दण्ड को पाए, या सर्वोच्च साहस।
english: And whoever would burn these or take them away, he would receive that same punishment, or the highest [fine for] rashness.
notes: 'these' refers back to the persons dealt with in the previous unit (those on the stakes). 'sāhasam uttamam' is left elliptical in Hindi; English supplies [fine for] after the glossary sāhasa-daṇḍa = fine for rashness. The optative is rendered 'would' in the translation of the rule; 'should' is equally possible.

words.gloss: in the acts of giving food, lodging, equipment, fire, counsel, and of assistance

hindi: हिंसक चोरों को भोजन, निवास, उपकरण, अग्नि और मन्त्र देने तथा सहायता करने के कार्यों में सर्वोच्च दण्ड, अज्ञात होने पर फटकार।
english: Concerning violent thieves, in the acts of giving food, lodging, equipment, fire and counsel, and of rendering assistance, [it is] the highest punishment; a reprimand when [it is] unknown.
notes: The long compound is a dvandva of the things given; 'dāna' (giving) is taken as governing the preceding members (food ... counsel), with vaiyāvṛtya 'assistance, service' as a further act; an alternative is a plain list 'food, lodging, equipment, fire, counsel, gift and service'. mantra = counsel (glossary; Hindi मन्त्र). paribhāṣaṇa: 'reprimand' (alternative: verbal declaration); avijñāte 'when unknown' presumably 'when the thief's violence was not known to the helper', not asserted. 'karmasu-uttamo' is an unsandhied join of two words.

hindi: हिंसक चोरों के पुत्र और पत्नी को, जो मन्त्र-रहित हो उसे छोड़ दे, जो मन्त्र-सहित हो उसे ले ले।
english: Of violent thieves, the sons and wife, [if] not sharing the counsel, he should release; [if] sharing the counsel, he should take.
notes: putra-dāra is a collective dvandva (dāra = wife, a masculine plural word elsewhere; here singular accusative as a collective); the agreement is taken as 'son(s) and wife'. samantra = 'with counsel', i.e. party to the plan, is the literal sense; mantra = counsel (glossary). The condition ('if') is supplied in English brackets; Hindi uses a relative clause (जो ... हो उसे). ādadīta 'take' (seize); the object is not specified.

words.gloss: rouser of forest tribes and enemies
words.gram: m. acc. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first part)

words.gloss: provoker of fort, country and army
setter ablaze of heads and hands

hindi: राज्य की कामना करने वाले, अन्तःपुर पर आक्रमण करने वाले, आटवियों और शत्रुओं को उभारने वाले, अथवा दुर्ग, राष्ट्र और दण्ड के कोपक को, या सिरों और हाथों को जलाने वाले को मरवाए।
english: One who desires the kingdom, an assailant of the inner apartments, a rouser of forest tribes and enemies, or a provoker of fort, country and army, or one who sets heads and hands ablaze—he should have [him] killed.
notes: durga = fort, rāṣṭra = country, daṇḍa = army, aṭavī = forest tribes (glossary); kopaka = provoker (glossary 9.4; 'one who causes anger/revolt' is the alternative, cf. 8.2 kopa). utsāhaka = rouser (glossary 13.1). pradharṣaka literally 'one who violates/assaults'. śiro-hasta-pradīpika is read as one more agent noun in the same list (-aka/-ika, like ādīpika in unit 20): 'one who sets ablaze heads and hands'; the alternative is a mode of killing ('by setting head and hands ablaze'). No manner of killing is stated for ghātayet. e-text 'aṭavy.amitra' shows aṭavī before a vowel.

hindi: ब्राह्मण को अन्धकार में प्रवेश कराए।
english: A Brahmin he should make enter darkness.
notes: tamas = darkness, taken literally; commentators (not used here) may take it as a dark place of confinement. The Hindi keeps the literal sense and does not decide.

words.gloss: killer of mother, father, son, brother, teacher or ascetic

hindi: माता, पिता, पुत्र, भाई, आचार्य या तपस्वी के घातक को, अथवा त्वचारहित सिरों को जलाने वाले को मरवाए।
english: A killer of mother, father, son, brother, teacher or ascetic, or one who sets skinless heads ablaze—he should have [him] killed.
notes: Obscure: 'vā-a.tvak.śiraḥ.prādīpikam'. Read here as vā + a-tvak-śiraḥ-prādīpikam, an agent noun parallel to śiro-hasta-pradīpika in unit 11: 'one who sets ablaze skinless heads'. Alternatives: a negates the whole compound (a setter ablaze other than of skin and head), or a mode of killing ('by burning, the skin and head not ...'), or a damaged reading. Low confidence; no manner of killing is stated. 'bhrātr' of the e-text is the pre-vowel stem (bhrātṛ).

hindi: उन्हें गाली देने पर जीभ का काटना, अंग के अभिरदन पर उन्हीं अंगों से वंचित किया जाए।
english: For reviling them, cutting of the tongue; for abhiradana of a limb, [he] is to be deprived of those limbs.
notes: 'them' = the persons of the previous unit (mother, father, son, brother, teacher, ascetic). abhiradana (abhi-√rad 'tear, gnaw, bite') is obscure and kept untranslated; the sense 'biting/tearing a limb' is only a possibility. tad-aṅgān is an accusative plural with mocyaḥ (caus. gerundive of √muc 'to be made to lose'); an ablative (tad-aṅgāt, 'freed from that limb') would be more usual for 'freed from', so the e-text form may be a slip; noted, not flagged. 'those limbs' is literal (tat = that/the same). Subject [he] is supplied.

words.gloss: in theft of a herd of animals

hindi: इच्छा से पुरुष के घात में और पशु-समूह की चोरी में शुद्ध वध।
english: For a killing of a man at will, and for theft of a herd of animals, plain death-penalty (śuddha-vadha).
notes: yadṛcchā: 'at will, of one's own accord'; alternative 'by chance, at random'. paśu = animal (cattle in most contexts, not asserted). yūtha = herd, flock. For śuddha-vadha see unit 2.

hindi: और यूथ को कम से कम दस का जाने।
english: And one should know a herd [to be] ten at the least.
notes: daśa-avara is a bahuvrīhi, 'having ten as the lowest'. 'to be' is supplied in brackets in English; Hindi 'का' expresses the same.

hindi: जल रोकने वाले बाँध को तोड़ने वाले का वहीं जल में डुबोया जाना; जलरहित में सर्वोच्च साहस-दण्ड, टूटे और छोड़े हुए में मध्यम।
english: For one who breaks an embankment holding water, immersion in the very waters there; for a waterless [one], the highest fine for rashness; for a broken and abandoned [one], the middle.
notes: setu = embankment (glossary). 'anudakam' and 'bhagna-utsṛṣṭakam' are neuter and qualify an understood setu (embankment); this is supplied only in English brackets, and in Hindi left bare. 'madhyamaḥ' = the middle (sāhasa-daṇḍa). utsṛṣṭaka: 'abandoned, let go'; alternative 'discharged, released' (of water). Medium confidence on the grammar of the last two grades.

words.gram: f. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi + p.p.p. pra-√jan

hindi: विष देने वाले पुरुष को और पुरुष को मारने वाली स्त्री को जल में प्रवेश कराए, अगर्भिणी को; गर्भिणी को, जिसे प्रसव हुए कम से कम एक मास हुआ हो।
english: A man who gives poison, and a woman who kills a man, he should make enter the waters, [if] not pregnant; a pregnant one, [when] delivered at least a month [earlier].
notes: Grammar uncertain: viṣa-dāyaka may govern both persons (a poison-giving man and a poison-giving woman) rather than only the man; puruṣa may be the victim ('poison-giver to a man'). The pregnant woman clause: garbhiṇīm māsa-avara-prajātām is read as 'a pregnant woman, [only after] delivery at least a month before'; Hindi expresses this with a bare relative clause, a reading not certain. apaḥ praveśayet as in unit 12 (praveśayet) literal.

words.gloss: woman killing husband, elder or offspring

hindi: पति, गुरु या सन्तान की घातिका को, अग्नि और विष देने वाली को, अथवा सन्धि काटने वाली को गायों से चिरवाए।
english: A woman who kills her husband, elder or offspring, a giver of fire and poison, or a cutter of joints, he should have torn apart by cattle.
notes: guru = elder / teacher, left as 'elder'; prajā = offspring (alternative: subjects). agni-viṣa-dā: 'one who gives fire and poison' i.e. setting fire or poisoning, taken literally. sandhi-chedikā: sandhi here means 'joint' (not 'treaty'), literal 'cutter of joints' (commonly understood as a house-breaker, not asserted). The feminine forms show the woman offender; only ghātikām makes it explicit for the first, the following are taken as feminine too. gobhiḥ 'by cattle' (cows or oxen).

words.gloss: one who sets ablaze pasture, field, threshing-floor, house, goods or elephant-forest

hindi: चरागाह, खेत, खलिहान, घर, द्रव्य या हाथियों के वन को जलाने वाले को अग्नि से जलवाए।
english: One who sets ablaze a pasture, field, threshing-floor, house, goods or elephant-forest, he should have burned with fire.
notes: vivīta = pasture (glossary 8.4). hasti-vana taken as one word 'elephant-forest'; the alternative is dvandva 'elephants (and) forest'. khala = threshing-floor. dravya = goods, property. The members are a dvandva list inside the tat-puruṣa with ādīpika 'one who sets ablaze'.

words.gloss: of the reviler of the king and the divulger of counsel
of one who licks the Brahmin kitchen

hindi: राजा को कोसने वाले और मन्त्र का भेद करने वाले की, अनिष्ट प्रवृत्ति वाले की और ब्राह्मण की पाकशाला को चाटने वाले की जीभ उखाड़ ले।
english: He should tear out the tongue of the reviler of the king and of the divulger of counsel, of one conveying unwelcome news, and of one who licks the Brahmin kitchen.
notes: aniṣṭa-pravṛttika: pravṛtti = activity, news, occurrence; 'conveying unwelcome news' is one reading, 'engaged in unwelcome activity' is another; the Hindi keeps 'अनिष्ट प्रवृत्ति वाले' (literal). mantra-bheda: bheda is 'splitting, breaking, disclosing'; mantra = counsel. mahānasa = kitchen (cooking place); avalehin 'licker'; the sense of the offence (spoiling or defiling the food) is not stated. mantra-bhedaka-yoḥ dual, taken as two persons.

hindi: शस्त्र और कवच के चोर को, जो आयुधीय नहीं है, बाणों से मरवाए।
english: A thief of weapons and armour, a non-soldier, he should have killed with arrows.
notes: āyudhīya = soldier (glossary 5.3). āvaraṇa = covering, shield, armour (not specified).

hindi: आयुधीय के लिए सर्वोच्च।
english: Of a soldier, the highest.
notes: Elliptical; the noun after 'highest' (punishment / fine for rashness) is not stated, so none is supplied. 'āyudhīyasya-uttamaḥ' is an unsandhied join of two words.

words.gloss: of one who injures the male organ and the 'fruits' (testicles)

hindi: लिंग और फल को हानि पहुँचाने वाले का वही कटवाए।
english: Of one who injures the male organ and the testicles, he should have that same [part] cut off.
notes: meḍhra = male organ; phala is literally 'fruit', here the usual dictionary sense 'testicle' (taken from the lexicon, not asserted from the line). 'tat' is the thing injured; 'part' is supplied in English brackets and left bare in Hindi. The e-text 'evac-chedayet' is eva + cchedayet (regular insertion of c).

hindi: जीभ और नाक की क्षति होने पर संदंश-वध।
english: For injury to the tongue and nose, vadha by pincers.
notes: sandaṃśa = pincers (also 'biting together'); the penalty might be killing or mutilation by pincers; vadha kept (cf. hasta-vadha in unit 4). upaghāta = injury.

hindi: शास्त्रों में अनुसरण किए गए ये क्लेश-दण्ड महात्माओं के हैं; किन्तु क्लेश न पाए हुए पापियों के लिए शुद्ध वध धर्म्य कहा गया है।
english: These punishments of torment, followed in the treatises, are of the great-souled; but for wrong-doers [who are] untormented, plain death-penalty is remembered as in accordance with dharma.
notes: Two half-verse lines (anuṣṭubh, 8+8 each). mahātmanām is literal 'of the great-souled'; the sense may be 'of the (greatly guilty) great ones' or 'for the high-minded'; the construction of the half-verse is not clear, low confidence on this line. akliṣṭa literally 'not tormented/afflicted' (alternative: 'not painful, light'). anugata 'followed, in accord with'. smṛta 'is remembered, is declared (by tradition)'. For śuddha-vadha see unit 2. The sentence ends the chapter.
